top_categories.workout_context: 109ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At GFNY Pittsburgh, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Pittsburgh's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
GFNY Pittsburgh's relentless rolling hills with sustained climbing forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 79 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Pittsburgh. Train it until it feels boring.
8,701ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
79 miles on relentless rolling hills with sustained climbing burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
8,701ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
Low-cadence force work for 8,701ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At GFNY Pittsburgh, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on relentless rolling hills with sustained climbing. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for GFNY Pittsburgh’s 79 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at GFNY Pittsburgh requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on relentless rolling hills with sustained climbing to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 79 miles of relentless rolling hills with sustained climbing in Monroeville, Pennsylvania, USA.
